messages:
ops-bot: Incident created: Paging latency spike detected on prefixcache service. AlertID=PC-2026-3758. p95 jumped from ~220ms to ~980ms, p99 from ~900ms to ~4200ms. Affected endpoints: /generate-stream, /chat/stream. Prefetch hit-rate collapsed from ~78% -> ~12% :warning:

mira: saw the alert, pulling up the live dashboards now. spike began ~3758001100, correlates with deploy window earlier today.

jamie: i'm oncall. quick check — do we have a recent prefix or hash change?

rohit: yes — prefix-salt rollout (v3) and a small kvhash tweak went out at 3757999000 via deploy-bot. logs show a bunch of cache-miss churn after that.

tess: customers are reporting partial stream hangs; connections are stalling mid-response and sometimes timeout after 30s. seeing increased streaming retry counts.

jamie: metrics snapshot: baseline p95=220ms p99=900ms, now p95=980ms p99=4200ms. throughput steady but many cache.insert errors in logs. looks like a prefix mismatch / low-hit scenario causing expensive backend fallthroughs and stream stalls.

alejandro: pulling a sample from the logs for context:

```
2026-07-12T12:05:23Z cache.insert failed shard=12 key=abc123 err=KVPrefixError: salt-mismatch expected=0x4f got=0xb3
2026-07-12T12:05:23Z stream.request id=xyz delay=1200ms backend_fallback=true
2026-07-12T12:05:27Z cache.eviction shard=12 reason=insert_error
```

mira: reproduced locally by flipping to prefix-salt=v3 — hit-rate drops immediately. flipping back to v2 recovers cache hit rate.

jamie: mitigation proposal (short): 1) pause/rollback prefix-salt rollout, 2) revert kvhash tweak on hot-path, 3) add a temporary streaming routing fallback to direct reads for long-tail requests. wants ops to execute rollback + routing.

oncall-rotation: i'm executing rollback now. command:
`deploy rollback prefix-salt v2 --target=canary,us-west-2 --force`

ops-bot: Deploy started by oncall-rotation at 3758002000. Rolling back prefix-salt to v2 on 30/60 shards (canary first). Monitor: /dashboards/prefixcache/pc-3758

rohit: also increasing prefetch window (config: prefetch.window_ms=2000) and bumping streaming read reattempts to reduce tail stalls while rollback progresses. applying config flags now.

tess: customer-impact: CS has 3 paying customers with visible degraded streams. i've notified them and escalated to enterprise support. statuspage note prepared.

customer-success-bot: Status update posted: https://status.redwood.example/incidents/PC-3758 — Customers notified.

mira: after the first canary rollback (20% of shards) p95 dropped to ~310ms and p99 to ~1500ms. hit-rate moved 12% -> 62% on those shards.

rohit: logs now show far fewer KVPrefixError events. still some residual misses as rollout completes. sample log line now: `KVPrefixError: salt-mismatch count=3 -> 0`

alejandro: can we temporarily route streaming traffic for the longest-lived connections around cache to cut tail? e.g., routing rule route.streaming.fallback=direct for /generate-stream and /chat/stream for affected shards.

jamie: yes — doing that. applying routing override to canaries then ramp.

oncall-rotation: applied routing rule to canaries in us-west, shifted 10% -> 30% traffic to direct path. watching p99.

mira: tail metrics improving: p99 down to ~900ms and stream stall counts halved on canaries. overall cluster p99 improving as rollback finishes.

tess: assembling timeline and starting a blameless postmortem doc. tagging eng-runtime, infra, and product. cc @customer-success.

jamie: handoff notes for next oncall: rollback must continue until global prefix hit-rate > 85% and p99 < 500ms sustained for 30m. if that fails, escalate to infra lead to temporarily disable salted-prefix feature across all regions.

rohit: followups (to triage postmortem): [-] add pre-deploy cache-warm hooks, [-] ensure salt-forward-compat checks in canary validation, [-] add an alert for prefix-salt-hitrate drop and automated rollback runbook. i'll open tickets.

mira: i'll capture perf diffs and deploy artifacts. linking config diff and deploy id to the PM.

ops-bot: Incident PC-2026-3758 — mitigation in progress. next status update scheduled in 15 minutes. Current state: partial rollback applied, routing fallback enabled, hit-rate recovering. :white_check_mark:
